opportunities.title: Process mining is outgrowing the single file
opportunities.text: Process mining is outgrowing the single file Treating a dataset as a single file is a luxury of small scale. In object-centric process mining, events are tied to multiple objects. The current standards, JSON-OCEL and JSON-XML, handle this by packing everything into a file. To do anything useful, like discovering object-centric process models, you have to parse the whole thing. It is a bottleneck that forces researchers to treat massive, interconnected event logs as monolithic blobs. The move toward database-driven storage, as discussed in arXiv:2202.05639 regarding OCEL storage, shifts the problem from parsing to querying. opportunities.title: Functional correctness is a low bar for code generation.
opportunities.text: Functional correctness is a low bar for code generation. A compiler is not a security auditor. We have spent two years celebrating the fact that LLMs can write code that runs. If the syntax is valid and the unit tests pass, the industry treats it as a success. But in a governed ecosystem, "it works" is the beginning of the conversation, not the end. The EduPluginBench executable assurance study reveals the gap between functional parsing and systemic compliance. In a study of 600 unmodified generations from two current coding models, 300 parsed successfully. However, none passed P0 or achieved P0-P4 conformance.
